title: Speech of President Arroyo during the wreath laying ceremony and program in commemoration of the 23rd Death Anniversary of Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino, Jr.
text:
Speech of Her Excellency Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo President of the Philippines During the wreath laying ceremony and program in commemoration of the 23rd Death Anniversary of Benigno “Ninoy” Aquino, Jr.

[Delivered at the Ninoy Aquino Monument, P. Burgos cor. Roxas Blvd., Manila, August 21, 2006]

Maraming salamat.

Maraming salamat.

Maraming salamat, Mayor Lito Atienza at lahat ng namumuno, mamamayan at kabataan ng Maynila. Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat.

Binabati rin natin ang mga kapatid ng ating bayani, si Ninoy Aquino, sa pamumuno ni Congressman Butch Aquino, ni Former Senator Tessie Aquino, ni Paul Aquino, ni Lupita Aquino-Kashiwahara at saka ni Maur Aquino Lichauco.

Binabati natin ‘yung EDSA People Power Commission sa pamumuno ni Ed Ermita at ni Brother Rolando Dizon. Ganun din si Bert Romulo, si Toting Bunye, si Sonny Alvarez at ‘yung iba pang mga Cabinet member at kasapi ng ating administrasyon.

Binabati natin ‘yung mga kasamahan ni Ninoy sa kaniyang pakikibaka, nandiyan si Reli German at ‘yung ibang narito na napakarami ang dumalo ngayon, hindi ko na babanggitin lahat ng pangalan nila.

Batiin natin ‘yung spirit of EDSA sa pamumuno ni Cris Carreon at saka ‘yung nag-aalaga ng pangalan ni Ninoy sa ating kasaysayan, ang National Historical Commission sa pamumuno ni Executive Director Badoy.

Sa inyong lahat, mga humahanga kay Ninoy, mga susunod na henerasyon ng Maynila at Pilipinas, karangalan kong makidalo kasama ninyong lahat sa anibersaryo ng kamatayan ng ating bayani si Ninoy Aquino sa pamamagitan ng pagdala ng bulaklak sa kanyang dambana at pagkatapos magtanim ng yellow fire tree dito sa Maynila para mas lalong mabuhay ang Maynila at hindi lamang ang demokrasya.

Itong araw na ito, sinisimulaan din natin ang “Greening of Manila” ni Mayor Lito Atienza at mga kabataan ng Maynila. Di ba kayo ang magtatanim ng puno sa buong Maynila? Ito ay tugmang-tugma, tugmang-tugma sa inyong kinabukasan, tugmang-tugma rin sa bagong berdeng Pilipinas na inilulunsad ng pambansang pamahalaan kasama rin ng susunod na henerasyon.

Kasi kung gusto natin na maging first world ang ating bansa sa 2020, sa panahon ng susunod na henerasyon, yung henerasyong ipinagbaka ni Ninoy Aquino, kailangan ang higit na atensyon sa ating likas na kapaligiran at siguraduhin ninyo mga kabataan, palaguin natin at hindi lamang ubusin ang ating mga likas yaman.

Isa pang tanda ng modernong bansa na gusto maging first world ay katarungang panlipunan at karapatang pantao. Dahil itong araw na ito, naaalala natin na si Ninoy Aquino ay nagbuwis ng kaniyang buhay upang bumalik ang demokrasya. Si Ninoy Aquino ang pinaka-kilalang biktima ng political killing, at hanggang ngayon hindi pa natin alam kung sino ang mastermind ng pagpaslang kay Ninoy Aquino. Dapat lang hindi natin balewalain ang kaniyang sakripisyo.

Democracy in the Philippines will not stand for senseless political killings. Every man and woman in our country is entitled to speak, free from fear that they will pay for their beliefs with their very life. Whether you are a journalist or political activist, of the left or the right, it is the obligation of the government and indeed the entire nation to protect the rights and liberties of every citizen.

At kayo bilang mga tagahanga, tagahanga ni Ninoy Aquino — Thank you — bilang mga tagahanga ni Ninoy Aquino kaya tayo ay narito, mga nag-gugunita ng pagka-martir ni Ninoy Aquino na nakibaka para sa susunod na henerasyon. You know that for too long there has been a culture of violence in our political process. For years, political disputes have been settled looking down the barrel of a gun.

A week ago, I announced that I was going to appoint a Former Supreme Court Justice to investigate the recent political killings. Today, in honor of the great victim of political killings, Ninoy Aquino, I am announcing that Former Supreme Court Justice Jose Melo will lead an investigative group imbued with wide power and a sweeping mandate for its members to put murderers behind bars and break this cycle of violence once and for all.

We’ve been making progress in bringing these cases to court and putting the killers behind bars, but I’ve been impatient, we’ve been impatient with the pace. That is why we took the step of appointing Melo. He will be joined by NBI Director Nestor Mantaring and Chief State Prosecutor Jovencio Zuño and members of civil society including Bishop Camilo Gregorio of the catholic church and Rogelio Vinluan as senior counsel and Nelia Gonzalez in the legal and academic community.

I have directed Melo to prioritize and focus investigation of media and activist killings; to be the government’s sole voice on the issue; and to make a report to me outlining its actions and policy recommendations including appropriate prosecution and legislative proposals, if any, aimed at eradicating the root causes of extra judicial killings and breaking the cycle of violence once and for all.

I have directed him to leave no stone unturned in their pursuit of justice. I want them to pursue every lead down every path. The victims and their families deserve justice to be served; the Filipino people for whom Ninoy died fighting for democracy deserve a democracy they can trust.

It’s time that the culture of political retribution stop. I hope that this special investigative commission will not only solve the killings before us today, but will propose permanent remedies to change this culture.

Ipagpatuloy natin ang sigla ng demokrasyang pinagbuwisan ng dugo, pawis at buhay ng ating magigiting na bayani tulad ni Ninoy. Sa ganitong paraan, hindi mauuwi sa wala ang sakripisyong inialay ni Ninoy para sa atin at sa bayan.

Sana ay tularan si Ninoy ng maraming magmalasakit para sa mahal nating bayan, lalung-lalo na ang ating susunod na henerasyon, ang kabataan ng Maynila at ng buong Pilipinas.

Mabuhay si Ninoy! Mabuhay ang Maynila! Mabuhay ang berdeng Ppilipinas!

Maraming salamat sa inyong lahat.
